ebitda.summary: EBITDA adds deducted interest, income tax, depreciation and amortization back to net income. For $80,000 net income, $10,000 net interest expense, $20,000 income tax and $30,000 D&A, EBITDA is $140,000. Against $500,000 revenue, the margin is 28%.
ebitda.scope: Unadjusted same-period earnings reconciliation in one currency. Signed losses, net-interest income and tax benefits are supported. Operating-income mode includes separately entered other nonoperating income or expense, excluding interest and tax. No cash-flow forecast, valuation or discretionary adjusted-EBITDA addbacks.

examples.title: Reconcile net income to a 28% margin
examples.inputs: net_income: 80000; interest: 10000; income_tax: 20000; depreciation: 20000; amortization: 10000; revenue: 500000

examples.title: Include nonoperating income in the operating bridge
steps: Operating income 105,000 plus other nonoperating income 5,000 gives EBIT 110,000.
Add 30,000 D&A to recover the same 140,000 EBITDA. Interest and income tax are not added again.

examples.title: Preserve a loss and a tax benefit
examples.inputs: net_income: -50000; interest: 5000; income_tax: -10000; depreciation: 10000; amortization: 0; revenue: 200000
steps: Start with a loss of 50,000. Add interest expense 5,000, subtract the 10,000 income-tax benefit, then add 10,000 depreciation.
EBITDA is −45,000; margin on 200,000 revenue is −22.5%.

questions.question: Is EBIT the same as EBITDA?
questions.answer: No. In the example EBIT is 110,000 and D&A is 30,000, making EBITDA 140,000.

questions.question: Can EBITDA be negative?
questions.answer: Yes. Losses and signed tax or interest benefits can produce negative EBITDA. The calculator preserves that loss.

questions.question: Can I use this as adjusted EBITDA?
questions.answer: The worksheet does not add back discretionary costs or infer a lender’s adjustments. Such definitions need their own reconciliation and clear labeling.

invoice-factoring.summary: A factoring advance is part of the invoice proceeds, not extra revenue. On a $10,000 invoice with an 80% advance, 2% per 30 days prorated for 45 days and $50 other fees, you receive $8,000 today and $1,650 at settlement: $9,650 in total.
invoice-factoring.scope: One fully collected invoice, one advance today and all fees deducted at collection. Select invoice-face or advance fee base, a constant per-interval rate, prorated or started intervals and separately entered other fees. No default, recourse, upfront deductions, statutory APR, lender quote or financing approval.

examples.title: Prorate a 45-day fee interval
examples.inputs: invoice: 10000; advance_rate: 80; fee_rate: 2; interval: 30; days: 45; billing: Prorated periods; fee_base: Invoice face value; other_fees: 50
examples.answer: Total net proceeds: 9,650.00 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Charge every started period
examples.inputs: invoice: 10000; advance_rate: 80; fee_rate: 2; interval: 30; days: 45; billing: Started periods; fee_base: Invoice face value; other_fees: 50
steps: The advance stays 8,000, but final settlement falls to 1,550.
examples.answer: Total net proceeds: 9,550.00 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Fees exceed the reserve
examples.inputs: invoice: 10000; advance_rate: 99; fee_rate: 2; interval: 30; days: 30; billing: Prorated periods; fee_base: Invoice face value; other_fees: 0
steps: A 99% advance pays 9,900 today and leaves a reserve of 100.
The 30-day fee is 200. Settlement = 100 − 200 = −100: another 100 is owed.
examples.answer: Signed settlement after fees: -100.00 under these assumptions.

sources.title: 1st Commercial Credit: invoice factoring calculator and input definitions

questions.question: Is the advance extra income?
questions.answer: No. It is an early payment of part of the invoice proceeds. Adding it again to the full invoice after fees double counts it.

questions.question: Are factoring fees always based on invoice face value?
questions.answer: Contract terms differ. This tool supports the entered invoice-face or advance-amount fee base and an explicit interval rule.

questions.question: Does this calculator determine APR or approval?
questions.answer: No. It shows cash timing and specified charges for one fully collected invoice. It does not quote finance terms or determine eligibility.

average-daily-balance.summary: Average daily balance weights each daily balance by how long it lasts. A $500 balance for 9 days, $700 for 10 days and $400 for 11 days totals 15,900 balance-days. Over 30 days, the average is $530; at 24% / 365, estimated simple interest is $10.45.
average-daily-balance.scope: Single-balance, inclusive-date or consecutive segment worksheet. Posting-day changes count that day and same-day changes combine. Signed credit balances are retained. Optional simple interest uses max(ADB, 0), one entered APR and a 360/365 divisor; no grace periods, daily compounding, multiple APR buckets or exact issuer bill.

examples.title: Weight a purchase and payment by posting date
examples.answer: Average daily balance: 530.00 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Restore the equivalent consecutive segments
steps: The three segments cover 9 + 10 + 11 = 30 days exactly.
examples.answer: Estimated simple cycle interest: 10.45 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Combine transactions on the same posting day
steps: The purchase 200 and payment −300 both post November 10, a net −100.
examples.answer: Average daily balance: 430.00 under these assumptions.

sources.title: CFPB: how credit-card interest is calculated
CFPB: daily periodic rate and 360/365 divisors

questions.question: Do payments reduce the average immediately?
questions.answer: In this worksheet, a payment reduces the balance from its posting date, including that day. Use the actual posting date rather than the initiation date.

questions.question: What if two transactions post on the same day?
questions.answer: Their signed amounts are combined before that day’s balance is counted. Input order does not change the result.

questions.question: Can I use ADB for a savings-account fee requirement?
questions.answer: You can calculate a weighted balance, but minimum-balance, qualifying deposit and fee-waiver rules depend on the bank. This tool does not decide eligibility.

construction-loan.summary: Construction interest depends on funds actually drawn. With $50,000 drawn November 1 and another $50,000 November 16, the average outstanding balance for November is $75,000. At 12% on an actual/365 basis, 30 days cost $739.73 before separately paid fees.
construction-loan.scope: Constant-rate, interest-paid-separately construction period with dated nonnegative draws, opening principal and a commitment ceiling. Includes draw day and final day; actual calendar days divided by chosen 360/365. No principal repayments, interest capitalization, land equity, approval or permanent mortgage stage.

examples.title: Two draws across a 30-day construction period
examples.answer: Total construction interest: 739.73 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Choose an actual/360 rate convention
steps: Use the same draw timeline and divide actual days by 360 instead of 365.
Interest = 2,250,000 × 0.12 / 360 = 750. Add separately paid fees of 1,000 for cost of 1,750.
examples.answer: Interest plus entered fees: 1,750.00 under these assumptions.

examples.title: Delay the second draw to the final day
steps: 50,000 lasts 29 days, then 100,000 lasts one day.
examples.answer: Total construction interest: 509.59 under these assumptions.

sources.title: CFPB: construction loan advances and repayment choices

questions.question: Are fees included in the drawn principal?
questions.answer: No. All entered fees are paid separately; they are included in interest-plus-fee cost once and never earn interest.

questions.question: Can I capitalize interest or repay principal during construction?
questions.answer: This release assumes separately paid simple interest and no principal repayments. Those different cash-flow conventions need another model.

questions.question: Is this a preapproval calculator?
questions.answer: No. The commitment is a user-entered limit, not a lender’s eligibility or credit decision.
